title: Ramzan Ali v. State of U.P.
coram: V.K. Shukla, J.; Mohd. Tahir, J.
docket: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 2722 of 2015
disposition: s.135 FIR not quashed; CrPC 41/41-A on arrest; compounding under Code 2005.
headnote: Ramzan Ali sought quashing of a s.135 Electricity Act FIR (Case Crime No. 561 of 2014, P.S. Mughalsarai, Chandauli). The Division Bench held the FIR disclosed a cognizable offence and refused to quash it. Arrest had not been made. If arrest were contemplated for an offence not entailing more than seven years' imprisonment, police must comply with CrPC ss. 41(1)(b) and 41-A. If the offence is compoundable, the petitioner may seek the remedy under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Ramzan Ali petitioned the Allahabad High Court to quash an FIR dated 28 December 2014, registered as Case Crime No. 561 of 2014 under Section 135 of the Electricity Act, 2003 at Police Station Mughalsarai, District Chandauli. Counsel for the State and the U.P. Power Corporation appeared. He had not been arrested. Counsel argued that the alleged offence could not attract more than seven years' imprisonment, so arrest should not be mechanical, and that the offence was compoundable.

holding_units.topic: s.135 FIR quash; arrest safeguards; compounding
holding_units.holding: An FIR under s.135 of the Electricity Act, 2003 that discloses a cognizable offence is not to be quashed. Where arrest has not been made, apprehension of a breach of CrPC ss. 41(1)(b) and 41-A does not warrant interference; if arrest is contemplated for an offence not entailing more than seven years' imprisonment, police shall comply with those provisions. If the offence is compoundable, the accused may seek the remedy provided under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

not_decided.point: Compounding of the s.135 offence on merits
not_decided.note: Court did not compound or decide compoundability; petitioner may seek the Supply Code, 2005 remedy if the offence is compoundable.
